about.text: Cheese whose milk is set mainly by lactic acid after a day or more at cool room temperature, with only a trace of rennet; the curd is ladled into moulds, drains by itself and is often ash-coated and mould-ripened for a few weeks.

Mostly French goat’s cheeses: a few hundred thousand tonnes of cheese, at about 6 kg of milk a kilo. My own rough estimate.

facts.v: Whole raw goat’s milk in Sainte-Maure de Touraine AOP

picks.why: Iconic Loire goat-cheese log with a rye straw, PDO-protected and among France's best-known chèvres.
Famous Loire goat cheese from Sancerre country, PDO since 1976 and eaten young or aged.
Dauphiné's creamy cow's-milk cheese, PGI-protected and one of France's best-loved ripened lactic cheeses.
Distinctive ash-dusted truncated pyramid from Berry, PDO since 1998 and a symbol of French goat cheese.
Spicy PDO goat cheese of the Drôme and Ardèche, a defining cheese of the Rhône hills.
